events.title: Apple I goes on sale
events.summary: Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak began selling the Apple I computer kit in July 1976 — a single-board machine with 4 KB [RAM] and MOS 6502 [CPU].
events.about: The Apple I was a fully assembled motherboard — buyers added a keyboard, power supply, and case. The Byte Shop ordered 50 units, proving a market existed between Altair kits and finished systems. Wozniak's elegant design foreshadowed the Apple II; hobbyists got a working computer without weeks of soldering.

narrative.whyChosen: The Apple I was Apple's first product and bridge from hobby kits to the Apple II.
narrative.whyImportant: It validated that a polished [microcomputer] design could sell through retail channels.
narrative.problemSolved: Hobbyists wanted a working [CPU] board without building from scratch like the Altair.
